topic: Claude Code Weekly Limits Promotion: What It Means for Heavy Users

key_points: Authoritative statement: the promotion ran May 13 - Sep 13, 2026 and raised weekly Claude Code limits by 50%.
Anthropic planned to revert to original levels but made part of it permanent: from Sep 14, 2026 weekly limits are 25% higher than pre-promotion for Pro, Max, Team, and legacy seat-based Enterprise.
Eligibility: automatic, no action required; Free plans and consumption-based Enterprise seats were excluded.
Scope: Claude Code only, everywhere (CLI, IDE extensions, desktop, web); Claude chat and Claude Cowork limits unchanged.
5-hour session limits were NOT affected by the promotion; /usage in the CLI showed the updated limits.
Anthropic teases 'a lot more in the works around usage, visibility, and control'.
Framing critique: baseline 100 -> promo 150 -> permanent 125, i.e. 25% above baseline but ~17% below the promotional peak.
Anthropic deleted its original X thread and posted a clarification admitting: 'Compared to today, this works out to a 17% reduction in weekly limits on Claude Code.'
Weekly allowance is not a fixed prompt count - it varies with conversation length, model choice, tool usage, and effort level.
Anthropic says more usage changes are coming for better visibility and control.
Usage limits are a 'conversation budget' over a time period; drivers are conversation length/complexity, features used, model chosen, and effort level.
All Claude product surfaces (claude.ai, Claude Code, Claude Desktop) draw on the SAME usage limit - not separate pools.
Paid plans (Pro, Max, Team, seat-based Enterprise) can raise effective capacity by purchasing usage credits; consumption-based Enterprise is metered on consumption.
Length limits are separate: they are the context window, not the plan allowance (a distinction heavy users conflate).
Usage credits let Pro, Max 5x, and Max 20x subscribers keep working after hitting included limits, billed at standard API rates.
Enable via Settings > Usage > Usage credits on claude.ai, then prepay ('Add funds'); auto-reload available.
Controls: monthly spending cap, auto-reload threshold, usage alerts; there is a daily redemption limit of $2000.
Credits are billed separately from the subscription and show up as additional charges.
Enterprise benchmark: average ~$13 per developer per active day and $150-250 per developer per month; below $30 per active day for 90% of users.
/usage shows plan usage bars, a Day/Week toggle, activity stats, and a usage breakdown; the 'Session' block is API-oriented and not the subscription allowance.
When the usage endpoint is rate limited, /usage (v2.1.208+) shows last-known bars from the past 60 minutes with a 'Showing last-known usage' note; press r to retry.
Usage-credits row appears in /usage only while credits are on; /usage-credits (v2.1.211+/2.1.248+ for Enterprise) opens the right settings page by role.
/insights analyzes up to 200 recent sessions and writes ~/.claude/usage-data/report.html.

Official reduction playbook: manage context proactively, choose the right model, cut MCP overhead, move instructions from CLAUDE.md to skills, adjust extended thinking, delegate verbose work to subagents, manage agent-team token costs.
Field case study: routing non-reasoning 'I/O' work to a cheaper worker model cut Claude Code token usage by 90%.
Framing that resonates with heavy users: most agent work is I/O (reading files, generating boilerplate, updating docs), not reasoning.

Cited market data: a quarter of engineering leaders already spend $200-500 per developer per month on tokens, some past $2000; by 2028 AI coding costs are expected to exceed the average developer salary.

stats.fact: Weekly Claude Code limits were +50% during the promotional window May 13 - Sep 13, 2026 (extended repeatedly through the summer).

Since Sep 14, 2026 weekly limits are permanently 25% higher than the pre-promotion baseline for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise - which is ~17% lower than during the promotion (baseline 100 -> promo 150 -> permanent 125).
Anthropic publicly conceded the cut: 'Compared to today, this works out to a 17% reduction in weekly limits on Claude Code.'
The promotion never touched 5-hour session limits, and applied only to Claude Code - Claude chat and Cowork limits were unchanged.
On May 6, 2026 Anthropic doubled Claude Code's 5-hour window limits for Pro/Max and removed the peak-hours limit reduction, tied to a SpaceX Memphis data-center compute deal.
Usage of claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Desktop counts against ONE shared usage limit; API keys are metered per token instead.
Usage credits bill overage at standard API rates; daily redemption limit is $2000, with monthly spend caps and auto-reload thresholds configurable.
Enterprise benchmark: ~$13 per developer per active day and $150-250 per developer per month, under $30/active day for 90% of users.
Claude Pro is $20/month ($17/month billed annually); Max starts at $100/month with 5x and 20x tiers.
Reported heavy-user failure mode: a Max 20x user burned 9.6B tokens across 34 sessions in 7 days (Sep 16-22, 2026) and exhausted the weekly limit in ~2.5 days, 93.9% of usage on Opus 5.
Reported accounting shift: weekly consumption rate rose ~3.6x after the Sep 25, 2026 reset (93 responses per 1% before vs ~30 after) on an unchanged workflow.

Subagent fan-out is a documented allowance killer: one report had ~70% of a weekly Fable 5.1 allowance burned mostly on subagents killed by the rate limit; another burned 39% of a Max 20x weekly limit in under 24h via ~16 max-effort reviewer subagents.
The status-line JSON exposes only five_hour/seven_day windows, so per-model weekly limits (e.g. Fable) stay invisible until they bite - an open feature request as of Sep 29, 2026.
Expired prompt cache forces large re-caches (reports of ~800k tokens in one message) that land on both the 5-hour and weekly meters.
Anthropic's model cadence changed per-model limit math in Sep 2026: Fable 5.1 / Mythos 5.1 (Sep 1), Opus 5.5 (Sep 22), Sonnet 5.5 (Sep 28).
Routing non-reasoning I/O work to a cheaper model cut one team's Claude Code token usage by 90%; a quarter of engineering leaders already spend $200-500/developer/month on tokens, some above $2000.

angles: The promotion is over - lead with the honest math heavy users actually feel: 25% above the pre-May baseline, ~17% below the summer peak, and 5-hour limits never changed.
Reframe the October 2026 story: the limit that hurts now is not the promotion but per-model weekly caps (Fable 5.1 vs Opus 5.5 vs Sonnet 5.5) that the status line cannot even show.
Evidence-driven 'why does my limit drain so fast' section: prompt-cache expiry re-caching, subagent fan-out on premium models, long contexts, and shared allowances across claude.ai/Desktop/Code.

Practical stretching playbook with official levers (context management, model choice, MCP overhead, CLAUDE.md->skills, extended thinking, subagent discipline) plus /compact, /clear, and off-peak work.

Exit ramps when the cap hits: wait for reset vs enable usage credits (API rates, $2000/day redemption cap, set a monthly spend cap) vs upgrade 5x->20x (with the caveat that reported upgrade-timing bugs mean you should verify the meter after switching).
Plan/ROI math for heavy users grounded in the official enterprise benchmark (~$13/developer/active day, $150-250/month).
Monitoring angle: /usage Day/Week toggle and last-known snapshot behavior, /insights reports, status-line windows, and third-party trackers - and what each one cannot see.
